instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.

Cut the chicken into 1 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Transfer them to a bowl and add 1/4 tsp of the chili powder, the turmeric, the pepper, 3/4 tsp of the garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss and leave it while you chop.
Chop the onion and the tomato. Grate 1 tbsp ginger, mince the garlic, and slice the shallots thin.
Heat 2 tbsp of the coconut oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Add the fennel seeds. After about 20 seconds they will sizzle and smell sweet.
Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until golden. Don't rush the onion. That's where the flavor starts.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute, until the raw smell is gone. Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes, until it breaks down.
Add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it is white all over.
Turn the heat to medium. Stir in the coriander, the remaining 1 1/4 tsp garam masala and the remaining 1/4 tsp chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add 1/4 cup hot water, cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 2 minutes, until pink. Add the curry leaves and stand back a little. They will spatter. Cook for 30 seconds, until crisp. Take the pan off the heat.

Uncover the chicken and pour in the coconut milk. Add 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 5 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thick. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest piece, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink and the juices run clear.
Pour the shallots and curry leaves, with their oil, over the curry.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (Kerala Chicken Curry, 5 from 202) is the lead: a seasoned chicken, onion, ginger and garlic with tomato, a Kerala garam masala, thin coconut milk added once the chicken is nearly tender, and a coconut oil tempering of shallots and curry leaves. Its own shortcut is used here: store-bought garam masala and ground coriander in place of grinding a fresh blend, with the fennel seeds from its blend bloomed in the oil. Boneless thighs cook in about 10 minutes, where the lead uses bone-in pieces; the dried red chilies in the tempering are left out to keep it mild. Only one source was readable, so there is no second version to compare.
